title: 2007 AMC 10B Problem 22
statement: A player chooses one of the numbers \(1\) through \(4.\) After the choice has been made, two regular four-sided (tetrahedral) dice are rolled, with the sides of the dice numbered \(1\) through \(4.\) If the number chosen appears on the bottom of exactly one die after it is rolled, then the player wins \(\$1.\) If the number chosen appears on the bottom of both of the dice, then the player wins \(\$2.\) If the number chosen does not appear on the bottom of either of the dice, the player loses \(\$1.\) What is the expected return to the player, in dollars, for one roll of the dice?

solutions.text:
Each die shows the chosen number on the bottom with probability \(\dfrac14.\) So the number appears \(0,\) \(1,\) or \(2\) times with probabilities \(P(0)=\dfrac{9}{16},\ \) \(P(1)=\dfrac{6}{16},\ \) \(P(2)=\dfrac{1}{16}.\)

The expected return is \((-1)\cdot\dfrac{9}{16}\) \(+(1)\cdot\dfrac{6}{16}\) \(+(2)\cdot\dfrac{1}{16}\) \(=\dfrac{-9+6+2}{16}\) \(=-\dfrac{1}{16}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Each die independently shows the chosen number on the bottom with probability \(\dfrac14\)
Weight the payoffs \(-1,\) \(+1,\) and \(+2\) by the probabilities of \(0,\) \(1,\) and \(2\) matches
